episodes.title: The Lantern on the Broken Pier
episodes.summary: Dan, Bori, and Haeon begin their first day on the little island beside its worn-out pier. The lantern Seorin brought is lit, and the first voyage journal begins.

episodes.title: A Place for Everything
episodes.summary: When their first wood and stone get wet in the rain, the three residents organize the warehouse. They give everything a place and set aside wood for the next morning.

episodes.title: One Empty Bed
episodes.summary: The island's first house gets a bed and a shelf for visiting workers. No guest has arrived yet, but the empty room with its two cups makes the island feel less lonely.

episodes.title: The Blue Cord Behind the Warehouse
episodes.summary: While expanding the warehouse, they discover a box tied with blue cord and a bundle of old letters. Haeon finds an erased port name and turns the box into a new mailbox.

episodes.title: A Knot for the Return
episodes.summary: At the finished pier, Seorin asks for one more mooring ring to shelter a boat from the wind. Dan listens to the people who use the pier and improves its welcome for returning ships.

episodes.title: The Weight of the First Cargo
episodes.summary: The three residents divide cargo and provisions aboard their first trading ship. Work on the island continues after departure as they wait to hear how the first trade goes.

episodes.title: A Brief Report from the Sea
episodes.summary: Seorin sends a report after meeting a ship flying a hook flag. Whatever the outcome, the crew continues safely while the island prepares for their return.

episodes.title: A Receipt from Haesol
episodes.summary: Mora checks the remaining cargo at Haesol and issues their first trade receipt. The island receives its first earnings and a notice offering help from local workers.

episodes.title: Yeoul's Straw Hat
episodes.summary: Yeoul, the first visiting worker, checks the working hours and the boat home. As they work together, the three residents hear stories of Yeoul's hometown, Saltflat.

episodes.title: A Port Name in an Empty Room
episodes.summary: After finishing the contract, Yeoul leaves a boarding pass and news of Saltflat. Haeon realizes the hometown has not disappeared; the boats that served it have stopped.

episodes.title: A Place for the Gold
episodes.summary: The three residents discuss what their ship and island need before spending their first earnings. Their choice of cargo space, sails, or defenses becomes part of the ship's new look.

episodes.title: Still the Same Ship
episodes.summary: The larger ship still carries traces of its first voyage and the work of everyone who helped. As departure preparations end, a trade request arrives from Yeondu in Saltflat.

episodes.title: The Warehouse by the White Hills
episodes.summary: In Saltflat, Seorin meets Yeondu, who is struggling with shipping costs. They discuss a steady trading arrangement and take aboard a letter for Yeoul.

episodes.title: Arriving in One Piece
episodes.summary: Thanks to Dan's dividers and Bori's wrapping, the tableware from Pottery arrives intact. Seorin finds a use for a cup left out of the sale because of its crooked handle.

episodes.title: A New Hat from Windneck
episodes.summary: After learning sail repairs in Windneck, Yeoul returns to the island on a new contract. After receiving a letter from an older sister and repairing the sail, Yeoul sets off for the next job.

episodes.title: Buying Prices, Selling Prices
episodes.summary: Comparing salt prices and freight charges, Haeon notices a recurring requirement to take a detour. The residents ask why shipments must pass through a distant Company warehouse when a shorter route exists.

episodes.title: The Word Temporary
episodes.summary: The Company says the detour is necessary because the route was temporarily closed after an old storm. They decide to check the route themselves, while a familiar form makes Haeon hesitate.

episodes.title: Setting the Table Three Times
episodes.summary: Busy feeding everyone else, Bori realizes her own meal has gone uneaten. The residents find a way for people to eat and rest even when their boats arrive at different times.

episodes.title: News Before Cargo
episodes.summary: Letters passed between ports reveal where a misclassified sluice part should have gone. A copy of Yeondu's shipping form still bears a name missing from the map: Fogferry.

episodes.title: Different Sails of the Same Color
episodes.summary: Another red-sailed ship helps Homeward escape a pirate pursuit. After learning to tell the flags apart, the residents send the helpful fleet a letter of thanks.

episodes.title: An Anchorage at Sea
episodes.summary: At Redanchor, a moving anchorage where crews live together across several ships, Seorin meets Garam. Ships listed as out of service are still carrying supplies to small ports.

episodes.title: Kindness Has Its Terms
episodes.summary: When Garam offers to guide the route, Seorin checks the safety terms as well as the price. The island's residents put the agreement into plain language and arrange to work with the fleet.

episodes.title: Stitches in a False Flag
episodes.summary: Red cloth from an attack and the trading records reveal how the Hook Gang disguised its ships. Some accusations are cleared, though the Red Sail Fleet still has incidents of its own to explain.

episodes.title: What to Throw Overboard First
episodes.summary: During a shared convoy, Garam gives up valuable cargo to help a boat falling behind. Seorin writes of a past rescue that also meant leaving cargo behind.

episodes.title: The Door Yeondu Kept Shut
episodes.summary: Yeondu refuses to open the warehouse to Garam, who once took its food by force. Garam acknowledges the damage that remains, despite recent good deeds, and agrees to discuss repayment.

episodes.title: Haeon's Stamp
episodes.summary: A stamp on an old shipping form prompts Haeon to admit having compiled the Company's closure list. Haeon begins rebuilding trust by sharing records that were wrong or never properly checked.

episodes.title: Names Listed as Absent
episodes.summary: The closure list reveals what happened when very different situations were marked with the same symbol. A reply brought by Soa describes the people still living in those ports and the boats they need.

episodes.title: One Piece from Every Port
episodes.summary: Records gathered across the ports reveal where sailing information leaked to the Hook Gang. They help Subin verify the originals while keeping copies in several places.

episodes.title: Cargo in Place of an Apology
episodes.summary: Garam arrives in Saltflat with grain and repair materials to begin making amends. Yeondu records only what has actually been delivered and checks the shipments still owed.

episodes.title: Evening Lights Beyond the Fog
episodes.summary: Guided by Soa, Seorin, Garam, and Subin carefully survey the side channel. Beyond the mist, the people of Fogferry are doing their evening work and waiting for the next boat.

episodes.title: Like First-Time Guests
episodes.summary: The people of Fogferry share the routines they have kept for years and the supplies they need now. The little island combines their small orders and completes its first formal trade there.

episodes.title: The Singing Reef
episodes.summary: The reef's mysterious song turns out to be waves sounding an old warning device. Marks beneath it point toward a forgotten warehouse that appears at low tide.

episodes.title: A Map of Lowtide Island
episodes.summary: Seorin and the crew mark their way back as they approach the warehouse uncovered by the falling tide. Beyond a door bearing a cooking-pot symbol, they find sealed chests and a large bell.

episodes.title: Gold and a Place at the Table
episodes.summary: The warehouse gold is a shared fund set aside to restore the shipping routes. The ports check the records together and divide it between pay for the expedition and route repairs.

episodes.title: A Use for a Broken Lens
episodes.summary: In place of the huge old lens, Uran tests small reflectors to light the side channel. Once the needed signals are clear, work begins on a lighthouse suited to the little island.

episodes.title: Stitching the Third Sail
episodes.summary: Skills from several ports come together in Homeward's third design. Dan makes a maintenance list others can read and begins handing over parts of the work.

episodes.title: The Window in the Lighthouse Beam
episodes.summary: A reflector adjustment moves the lighthouse beam away from Bori's window. A test ship answers the agreed signal, and the three residents watch its light together.

episodes.title: Where the Big Ship Stopped
episodes.summary: When the larger ship cannot enter shallow Reedbay, local small boats divide up its cargo. Haeon records a route that large ships and small boats can keep running together.

episodes.title: The Night the Map Changed
episodes.summary: Maps and revision orders kept by Isol reveal how the small ports were erased. Haeon compares the records and makes copies to send to the other ports.

episodes.title: Who Owns the Shortest Route?
episodes.summary: Dogyeom asks who will pay to maintain the route but does not explain the needless detours. Facing Company trade restrictions, the residents look for a way the ports can maintain their route together.

episodes.title: A Morning Without Orders
episodes.summary: Worried about Company penalties, merchants cancel orders on the new route. While keeping its existing trade going, the little island starts preparing a small market for direct sales.

episodes.title: The Crooked Market Sign
episodes.summary: The first market visitors arrive beneath a sign tilted by too many names. Small exchanges, repaired chairs, and traded goods fill the island's empty spaces.

episodes.title: The Fare Back Home
episodes.summary: The job notices Yeoul gathers leave out return fares and the length of each stay. The island sends out new notices covering lodging and the journey home as well as the work and pay.

episodes.title: A Receipt for an Unrepaired Lighthouse
episodes.summary: An expense record bears a completion stamp for lighthouse repairs that never happened. Mora and colleagues compare the supplies with the records and send the same evidence to the Company and the ports.

episodes.title: Dogyeom's Map
episodes.summary: At a meeting in Whitesail, Dogyeom cites a past rescue to defend control of the routes. Seorin and Soa present safety surveys and repair costs, but the meeting ends without agreement.

episodes.title: The Inspector's Empty Signature Line
episodes.summary: Subin refuses to sign an inaccurate report and takes on an independent inspection. Dan replaces a mooring ring flagged during the first visit to the island's pier.

episodes.title: One Task for Every Port
episodes.summary: Rather than gathering every job in one place, the ports divide the work according to their strengths. The little island takes responsibility for rest stops and passing on news, completing the shared plan.

episodes.title: An Old Ship's New Nameplate
episodes.summary: Homeward's fourth refit adds more cargo space and stronger defenses. Seorin and Dan keep the nameplate from the first voyage and prepare to share deliveries with smaller boats.

episodes.title: The Longest Receipt
episodes.summary: The first shared shipment passes between several ports and small boats. On the evening Subin recommends formal operation, a report arrives of a change in the southern wind.

episodes.title: This Time, Beforehand
episodes.summary: Observations from several ports point to a strong storm approaching. Everyone receives the same warning, and boats and supplies begin moving to shelter.

episodes.title: Close the Doors, Light the Lamps
episodes.summary: The island and ports follow their plan, checking boat positions and shelter preparations. As the three residents ready the signal chart and old lantern, answering lights appear offshore.

episodes.title: The Back of the Long Receipt
episodes.summary: Food, bowls, and repair supplies from the ports reach the sheltered boats. Bori and Haeon record who has received what and what is still needed.

episodes.title: Where the Hook Caught
episodes.summary: Gurok's false distress signal fails the agreed response check. The shared convoy guides merchant ships around it, while a patrol boat rescues Gurok's crew and arrests their captain.

episodes.title: When the Lighthouse Paused
episodes.summary: As wind and rain dim the lighthouse, the old lantern and neighboring ports keep the signals connected. After waiting safely, Dan repairs it with Yeoul and realizes the whole job need not rest on one person.

episodes.title: Names Returning Through the Reeds
episodes.summary: When news from a Reedbay work crew is late, Haeon asks for a local check instead of assuming an accident. Safe arrivals are confirmed one by one as the group completes its planned journey in small boats.

episodes.title: The Warehouse Doors at Whitesail
episodes.summary: Dogyeom sets aside the approval rules he created and opens the Whitesail warehouse to those seeking shelter. The other ports help with the rescue effort while continuing their claims over earlier losses.

episodes.title: Counting the Returning Ships
episodes.summary: As the rain eases, boats leave their prepared shelters and return to the little island. To the sound of the arrival bell, Haeon and the others call out each ship's name.

episodes.title: Correcting the Erased Entries
episodes.summary: A meeting settles Company responsibility, compensation, and independent route operation, and Dogyeom steps down. Haeon also shares the records from his own work, correcting them to distinguish a port's operating status from a person's address.

episodes.title: The First Homecoming Market
episodes.summary: People from many ports gather at the first Homecoming Market to share goods, skills, and news. When it ends, visitors return to their own boats, leaving the island with the memory of a day together.

episodes.title: A Place to Come Back To
episodes.summary: After the market, an ordinary boat arrives with cargo and letters. Welcoming new guests, the three residents write to the Island Keeper about all the new places to return to across the sea.

side_stories.title: Dan's New Hammer
side_stories.summary: Reluctant to use a new hammer, Dan watches a visiting carpenter at work. Dan tries the new tool and decides to keep using both hammers.

side_stories.title: A Short Reply from a Teacher
side_stories.summary: Dan sends pier measurements and a materials list to a former teacher. After reading the brief reply, Dan starts by asking the people who use the pier what they need.

side_stories.title: A Day Without Repairs
side_stories.summary: Even on a day off, Dan reaches to fix a seashell, then stops. Seeing repairs another carpenter has finished helps Dan learn how to rest.

side_stories.title: Bori's Unusual Soup
side_stories.summary: Bori puts ingredients from several ports into one pot, with disappointing results. While making a familiar soup again, she decides to try new ingredients one at a time.

side_stories.title: The Cookbook from a Closed Shop
side_stories.summary: Bori's old cookbook returns with notes from former customers. She realizes the shop she closed need not be remembered only as a failure.

side_stories.title: Time Booked in My Own Name
side_stories.summary: Bori puts time to browse the market on the preparation schedule. Leaving Dan in charge of the pot, she picks a plate for her own snack.

side_stories.title: Haeon's Untidy Handwriting
side_stories.summary: A letter Haeon copies in a hurry delivers its news in time. After reading Soa's reply, Haeon keeps the shaky handwriting as part of the record.

side_stories.title: A Gift at the Wrong Port
side_stories.summary: Haeon's thank-you gifts reach Pottery and Windneck the wrong way around. When the recipients find new uses for them, Haeon records both the mistake and its outcome.

side_stories.title: A Ledger Without an Eraser
side_stories.summary: While organizing a new ledger, Haeon realizes why old entries should be kept. Instead of erasing mistakes, Haeon adds the date and reason for each correction.

side_stories.title: Inside Yeoul's Hat
side_stories.summary: When the wind takes Yeoul's hat, boarding passes full of memories scatter across the ground. Yeoul leaves a few in the island's care before setting off for the next job.

side_stories.title: The Cargo Seorin Lost
side_stories.summary: A letter arrives from someone Seorin rescued long ago. Seorin accepts the connection that remained after the cargo was lost and hangs a small bell on the ship.

side_stories.title: The Margins of Mora's Ledger
side_stories.summary: Haeon finds symbols for greetings and personal news in the margins of Mora's ledger. Together, they write down the meanings so others can read them too.

side_stories.title: Yeondu's Letter Without Salt
side_stories.summary: At a younger sibling's request, Yeondu writes a letter about an ordinary day. The missing salt tally follows separately, giving personal news and work their own space.

side_stories.title: Garam's Loose Knot
side_stories.summary: When Garam tries to secure every crate of a repayment shipment alone, Yeondu calls a crew member over. Garam learns to record who is responsible and what was checked instead of doing every task personally.

side_stories.title: The Stars Uran Hadn't Seen
side_stories.summary: After focusing only on lighthouse brightness, Uran looks at the night sky from the other side. The route keeps its signal while less light spills into the residents' windows.

side_stories.title: Soa's Late Birthday Letter
side_stories.summary: Soa discovers a birthday letter left unsent for a long time. Sent at last with the current date added, it brings back old memories and a new drawing in reply.

side_stories.title: Isol's Blank Map
side_stories.summary: A child who cannot find home on a new map draws a route in the margin. Isol leaves space on the next map for people to add paths of their own.

side_stories.title: Subin's Holiday Inspection
side_stories.summary: Subin spends a day on the island without an inspection form. In a letter afterward, Subin writes of a good rest instead of inspection results.

ui.휴대폰 홈 화면에서 작은 섬의 하루를 바라보세요.\n\n작은 섬: 돌아오:
Watch a little island’s day unfold on your phone’s home screen.

Little Island is an Android live wallpaper game where residents gather resources and ships make trading voyages. Enjoy the island and sea on your home screen, then open the app to build and check your progress.

Gather wood and stone to prepare houses, a warehouse, and a dock. Ships depart from the dock, sell their cargo at a port, and return home. Pirate encounters resolve automatically, with the results recorded for you.

With a vacant lodging, you can welcome a worker to help. Workers gather resources alongside the residents for their agreed contract, then leave for their next destination.

When you return, a results card shows the progress made while you were away. Discover a little island that keeps moving without constant tapping.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper and build on your island.
ui.홈 화면에서 자라는 도트 섬, 자동 항해와 교역을 즐기고 돌아온 배의 이: Grow an island, send trading ships, and collect the stories they bring home.
ui.휴대폰 홈 화면에 작은 섬이 생겼어요.\n단은 나무를 모으고, 보리는 손:
A little island has appeared on your phone’s home screen.
Dan gathers wood, Bori prepares a place for visitors, and Haeon writes down news from returning ships. The island’s day goes on, even during a brief glance.

Little Island is an idle island-life game you can enjoy as a live wallpaper. Watch residents and ships on your home screen, then open the app to build and read the records you have gathered.

The feeling of a ship coming home
Gather wood and stone to build a dock and send out a trading ship. It sells cargo at a port, then returns to the island. Pirate encounters at sea resolve automatically. Check the results at your own pace when the ship comes home.

A place for guests to rest
Prepare a vacant room to welcome a worker. Visitors help for their agreed contract, then head to another port. Small rooms, cups, and lights on the pier gather stories of their own.

A journal to open when you like
From the first light to the first trade and the first guest, island life finds its way into the journal. Read a quick update or open the full story when you have time. Production and voyages continue either way.

A place that welcomes your own pace
There is no need to keep tapping or watching. Check the results of your time away when you return. Enjoy the island on your home screen, and open the app whenever you want to make a choice.

Join the island’s first voyage.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper, build, and browse your records.
ui.홈 화면에서 자라는 도트 섬, 항구를 잇는 자동 교역과 주민들의 긴 항해: Connect distant ports through idle sea trade and stories on your home screen.
ui.작은 섬에 불빛을 켜 주세요.\n배가 돌아오고, 편지가 도착하고, 멀리:
Light a lantern on a little island.
Ships come home, letters arrive, and stories connect faraway ports.

Little Island is an idle island-life game for your Android home screen. Care for the island where Dan, Bori, and Haeon live, send automatic trading voyages, and meet the ports of the Yeoul Sea. Build and choose routes in the app; enjoy the island’s scenery and brief news on your home screen.

Trade begins with an old boat
Load the wood and stone you have gathered and set out to sea. Discover different goods and trading partners at each port. Improve the cargo hold and sails of your own ship to reach wider routes. Pirate encounters resolve automatically and are recorded with the return results.

Changes that stay with the island
What began with spare rooms, a warehouse, and a dock grows to include a market and a lighthouse. Visiting workers stay for their agreed contracts and leave according to their own schedules. However the island grows, everyday life with Dan, Bori, and Haeon continues.

The mystery of a port erased from the map
A blue cord around a crate, an old boarding pass, a letter from far away. Ordinary trade leads to broken sea routes and promises between people. Read the main story, character side stories, and small voyage encounters whenever you like.

Stories on your own schedule
Production and voyages continue while the journal stays closed. Unread letters do not disappear, and reading late does not change the main story’s ending. Return to find the news and results that have gathered.

Life after coming home
After the story ends, collect seasonal decorations, enjoy harbor markets, and receive letters from returning visitors. Continue to the next voyage without losing your island or starting your ship’s growth over.

Bring a sea full of places to return to onto the home screen you visit each day.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper, build, select routes, and browse your records.

해금된 이야기 또는 항해 사건의 검증된 한 줄 소식.
정산 구간 지갑의 실제 순증감. 양수·음수·0을 모두 허용한다. 숫자 원자료에 부호 포함 축약 포맷을 한 번 적용하며 카드에 +를 덧붙이지 않는다.
해당 보급 사건에서 창고 한도를 넘어 실제로 보관하지 못한 나무와 돌의 합계. resources와 분리한다.

aggregation.economy_total_rule: 부재 요약은 정산 원장의 실제 증감 합계. 하위 판매·전투·귀항 금화를 다시 더하지 않는다.
aggregation.story_rule: 새 일지는 짧은 소식 한 줄만 덧붙이고 본문은 앱 안에 보관. 여러 외전은 편지 수로 묶는다.
aggregation.low_priority_rule: 창고·보급·생활 사건이 반복되면 최신 요약 한 건으로 합친다. 앱 기록은 모두 유지한다.
aggregation.payout_source: 게임 정산 원장. 전투 결과 원장의 확정 보상은 귀항 전까지 미지급 상태로 표시한다.
aggregation.story_storm_rule: 폭풍 본편은 고정 이야기 카드다. 일반 전투 확률, 부재 시간, 추가 피해 정산과 연결하지 않는다.
aggregation.trade_phase_rule: 기본 나무·돌은 방문항 판매 시 한 번 지급한다. 특산물은 출항 시 정수 가능 수량을 선결제 예약하고 방문항에서 선적한 뒤 귀항 시 작은 섬의 계약 수령선에 남은 수량을 인도하여 한 번 지급한다.
aggregation.combat_phase_rule: 전투 결과 카드에는 확정 보상만 기록한다. 금화는 귀항 정산 때 한 번 지급하며, 전투 카드 표시 시 잔액을 바꾸지 않는다.
aggregation.specialty_budget_rule: 예약량은 요청량·짐칸 한도·예산으로 살 수 있는 정수 수량의 최솟값. 양수 축소는 specialty_budget_low, 0개는 specialty_budget_empty 카드로 구분하며 기본 화물 항해는 계속된다.
aggregation.signed_amount_rule: 금화 순증감은 gold_delta의 부호 포함 표시를 그대로 넣는다. +{gold_delta}처럼 부호를 두 번 붙이지 않는다. gold는 순수 수입·보상 또는 비용 절대값에만 쓴다.
aggregation.overflow_rule: 보관 성공량 resources와 버린 양 overflow_resources는 별도 수량이다. 같은 공급량에서 각각 계산하고 요약에서 섞지 않는다.
aggregation.specialty_loaded_rule: specialty_bought 카드는 방문 생산항에서 실제 선적 완료 후에만 표시한다. 출항 선결제 시점에는 이 카드를 발행하지 않고 선결제 금화 내역만 기록한다.

release_profiles.title: Little Island
release_profiles.short_description: A cozy pixel island on your home screen, with gathering and automatic sea trade.
release_profiles.full_description:
Watch a little island’s day unfold on your phone’s home screen.

Little Island is an Android live wallpaper game where residents gather resources and ships make trading voyages. Enjoy the island and sea on your home screen, then open the app to build and check your progress.

Gather wood and stone to prepare houses, a warehouse, and a dock. Ships depart from the dock, sell their cargo at a port, and return home. Pirate encounters resolve automatically, with the results recorded for you.

With a vacant lodging, you can welcome a worker to help. Workers gather resources alongside the residents for their agreed contract, then leave for their next destination.

When you return, a results card shows the progress made while you were away. Discover a little island that keeps moving without constant tapping.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper and build on your island.

release_profiles.title: Little Island
release_profiles.short_description: Grow an island, send trading ships, and collect the stories they bring home.
release_profiles.full_description:
A little island has appeared on your phone’s home screen.
Dan gathers wood, Bori prepares a place for visitors, and Haeon writes down news from returning ships. The island’s day goes on, even during a brief glance.

Little Island is an idle island-life game you can enjoy as a live wallpaper. Watch residents and ships on your home screen, then open the app to build and read the records you have gathered.

The feeling of a ship coming home
Gather wood and stone to build a dock and send out a trading ship. It sells cargo at a port, then returns to the island. Pirate encounters at sea resolve automatically. Check the results at your own pace when the ship comes home.

A place for guests to rest
Prepare a vacant room to welcome a worker. Visitors help for their agreed contract, then head to another port. Small rooms, cups, and lights on the pier gather stories of their own.

A journal to open when you like
From the first light to the first trade and the first guest, island life finds its way into the journal. Read a quick update or open the full story when you have time. Production and voyages continue either way.

A place that welcomes your own pace
There is no need to keep tapping or watching. Check the results of your time away when you return. Enjoy the island on your home screen, and open the app whenever you want to make a choice.

Join the island’s first voyage.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper, build, and browse your records.

release_profiles.title: Little Island
release_profiles.short_description: Connect distant ports through idle sea trade and stories on your home screen.
release_profiles.full_description:
Light a lantern on a little island.
Ships come home, letters arrive, and stories connect faraway ports.

Little Island is an idle island-life game for your Android home screen. Care for the island where Dan, Bori, and Haeon live, send automatic trading voyages, and meet the ports of the Yeoul Sea. Build and choose routes in the app; enjoy the island’s scenery and brief news on your home screen.

Trade begins with an old boat
Load the wood and stone you have gathered and set out to sea. Discover different goods and trading partners at each port. Improve the cargo hold and sails of your own ship to reach wider routes. Pirate encounters resolve automatically and are recorded with the return results.

Changes that stay with the island
What began with spare rooms, a warehouse, and a dock grows to include a market and a lighthouse. Visiting workers stay for their agreed contracts and leave according to their own schedules. However the island grows, everyday life with Dan, Bori, and Haeon continues.

The mystery of a port erased from the map
A blue cord around a crate, an old boarding pass, a letter from far away. Ordinary trade leads to broken sea routes and promises between people. Read the main story, character side stories, and small voyage encounters whenever you like.

Stories on your own schedule
Production and voyages continue while the journal stays closed. Unread letters do not disappear, and reading late does not change the main story’s ending. Return to find the news and results that have gathered.

Life after coming home
After the story ends, collect seasonal decorations, enjoy harbor markets, and receive letters from returning visitors. Continue to the next voyage without losing your island or starting your ship’s growth over.

Bring a sea full of places to return to onto the home screen you visit each day.

This game uses Android live wallpaper. Follow the in-app guidance to apply the wallpaper, build, select routes, and browse your records.

localization_notes.scope: All user-facing strings in the three source documents. Developer-only planning prose is not a translation target; original result-card metadata is retained for structural fidelity.
localization_notes.layout_validation: Test English wrapping on the actual build; do not truncate parameter tokens or blindly apply Korean 18/25-character limits.
localization_notes.worker_term: Worker for island contracts; Crew for promoted sailors.
localization_notes.source_rename: Use Little Island for the app name; the story title remains a separate narrative title.
localization_notes.dictionary_context: Use ui_by_id when an exact Korean string has more than one context-specific English translation.

canonical_glossary.usage_note: Use Dock as the building label; pier is acceptable descriptive wording in story prose. Homeward and Seorin do not occur in the source UI display strings. Yeoul Sea occurs in the full-story store profile; the English core does not name the sea.

localization_notes.probability_unit: pp = percentage points; relative bonuses use %.
localization_notes.fallback: Look up stable IDs first. If an English entry is missing, retain the existing Korean source text rather than displaying an ID or an empty label.
localization_notes.narrative_scope: Main 60 and side 18: titles and summaries only. Full story bodies are outside this translation order.
localization_notes.integration_status: Data delivery only; English UI must be connected and layout-tested in the current app build.
